$Comment: Enchanter Orrin, standing in the Forgotten Temple at a spot of his own, away from the merchant
cluster where Sawyer Marn and the Mastery Trainer flank the Rootling merchant's marker. Orrin is
this pack's character end to end: his role, this placement and the conversation pressing F
opens all ship here, so a server without the pack has no enchanter to stand up. Interact names
a conversation rather than a screen because Orrin has quests to hand out and lines to say
before any list opens; a screen name there would open that screen with no conversation at
all. Author Open or Dialogue, never both.
To take Orrin out without editing this file, set Enabled false in
mods/ziggfreedcommon/npc-placements.json.
Where targets the temple by its GameplayConfig key rather than by name: that key is the
engine's own per-world gameplay-config id ('ForgottenTemple' ships with the base game) and
it is the same every time the temple is entered, while the world NAME carries a fresh uuid
each time.
Requires keeps Orrin away until the stations feature is on, which means RPG Stations is
installed and switched on; with it off his quests do not exist either, so nothing dangles.
Lifecycle keeps his chunk loaded, puts him back if something removes him, and raises his
health beyond anything that can be dealt. All three matter for a quest giver: a delivery
quest whose character is not standing where the player is parks unpaid until they find him.
This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS his role: the disenchanting
quests bind to Mmo_Enchanter, and any second placement of that role is the same enchanter,
offering and taking hand-ins for the same quests.
Anchor is the temple's own arrival spot plus an offset, the same anchor the Adventurer's Guide
uses for its temple standing (the guide stands fourteen blocks along negative X from the
arrival spot, on the open side of the landing; positive X runs into the structure). Orrin
stands between the arrival spot and the guide, eight blocks along negative X and two back
along negative Z, so he is clear of both the guide and the merchant cluster. To move him, edit
Anchor.WorldSpawn.Offset, keeping it small enough to stay out of the walls, and Yaw to turn
which way he faces; test the spot in game, since the walls do not move for the offset.
/mmonpc list --arg1=placements shows whether the placement resolved.
Name: Mmo_Enchanter_Temple
